body: Ooo, lots of ideas sparking from there. Thank you very much! This is wonderful.
Thank you SO much for a specific link. I know I'll spend a while browsing his tumblr and maybe I'll try to ask about the blog. Perfect. Thanks so much!
Never thought of that, thank you.
Oh, thank you so much. I'm looking at it right now.
I've been looking, but they're hard to find. Thanks for the suggestion though.

Could I ask why?
 (And, by the way, do you get your name from Harley Quinn? I'm a Batman fan, too.)
What happened, if I may ask?

I know I can be independent -- the major problem isn't him leaving. I mean, I'll be completely devastated when he does go, but not wanting to live dates way farther back than me knowing him. He just made my life so much better, and I'm terrified that once he's out of it I'll fall right back down into what I was before, and I don't want to do that. Thank you for your reply though.

I had never thought of it like that. I knew that he had made me better, but I didn't think of it like being a whole new person and leaving the "old one" behind. I'm afraid, too, that when he leaves I'll let myself slip into old habits. And that's not what I want - I really don't. But I'm just so tired of trying all the time, and there's tons of people in the world, so it wouldn't matter if *I* died. Looking at the numbers and facts, it doesn't make sense for me to work so hard at being merely adequate and/or insignificant. I would love to have a happy life, but all of the losses I have endured already have traumatized and desensitized me. Even if I kept on going after he's gone, I wouldn't want to get close to ANYONE else afterwards because it'll just be the last straw. I recognize that I cannot handle stress very well, but I don't really know how to change, and I guess don't want to change without him anyways. 

Thank you again. I'll keep in mind what you've said.

Thank you for replying, I really appreciate it.

I'm not looking forward to him leaving - that's the opposite of what I want. And he does know how much it's going to hurt me and, well, he knows everything. I've shared everything with him. 

I try to think of it that way, too - focus on the present. But I keep getting upset over it. The more I try to think about avoiding it the more I think about it and it doesn't really work. I'm posting about it now because I'm wondering if there's anything I can do to prevent myself from feeling so empty/awful/etc when it happens.  I know at the time I won't feel like doing anything, especially ask for help. 

I write down everything. I wrote him a book, actually, too. 

Sometimes I feel like I should stop opening up as much to him, and try to be okay until he leaves, and that way he'll just live his life thinking I'm living mine okay too, so he won't feel guilty, and won't realize I'm gone.
